newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italy donates vaccines to fight polio in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy donates vaccines to fight polio in Albania.

text.p: An emergency batch of vaccines to fight a polio outbreak that has claimed 12 lives in Albania since April arrived from Italy on Thursday, health officials said.
The first of two stages of an immunisation campaign for all Albanians up to the age of 50 will start on Monday and is expected to last two weeks.
Ibrahim Luloci, who heads the campaign, said the 3.4 million doses of vaccine worth $300,000 and donated by the Italian government had already been distributed to 10 regions.
"The distribution process is running smoothly for the vaccinations to start on Monday," Luloci said.
The Albanian Health Ministry has mobilised emergency helicopters to distribute the vaccine to more remote regions, he said.
The second stage of the vaccination campaign is scheduled to start in mid-November.
The World Health Organisation (WHO) and the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) appealed on Wednesday for $1.3 million to fund the emergency campaign.
WHO said 12 people had died and 78 had been infected so far in an outbreak which started in April but had not yet peaked and was showing signs of spreading to neighbouring countries.
